author: original (NevaIB)
title: Populations, samples and data

points.text: Population, sample, random sample; discrete and continuous data
Reliability of sources and bias in sampling
Sampling methods and how well they work

bigPicture: Statistics is only as good as its data. Before calculating anything, ask who was measured, how they were chosen, and whether any value looks wrong.

keyIdeas.cue: Population vs sample; discrete vs continuous data?
keyIdeas.answer: Population: everyone or everything of interest. Sample: the part measured. Random sample: every member has an equal chance of selection. Discrete data are counted (pets per house); continuous data are measured (height).

keyIdeas.cue: What makes data reliable, and where does bias come from?
keyIdeas.answer: Reliable data come from a trustworthy source, with a sample large and representative enough. Bias comes from who is chosen (e.g. only volunteers or friends), how questions are asked, or missing responses.
An outlier lies below Q1 − 1.5·IQR or above Q3 + 1.5·IQR. Investigate it: remove it only if it is an error; a genuine extreme value stays in the data.

keyIdeas.cue: Which sampling methods must you know?
keyIdeas.answer: Simple random, convenience, systematic (every kth item), quota (fixed numbers from each group, not random) and stratified (random within groups, in proportion to group size). Be able to judge how representative each is.

keyTerms.def: a systematic tendency to over- or under-represent
random selection within groups, sized in proportion

workedExamples.title: Stratified sizes
workedExamples.prompt: A school has 240 Year 12 and 360 Year 13 students. A stratified sample of 50 is taken.

misconceptions.right: Only remove values shown to be errors.
Quota sampling fills fixed numbers by convenience; stratified sampling is random within each group.

practice.prompt: A club has 120 juniors and 200 seniors. A stratified sample of 40 members is chosen. How many juniors and seniors are in the sample?
The data are 3, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 41. Find Q1 and Q3 and determine whether 3 or 41 are outliers.
